name: Fraser T Smith
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 pop-2020s — Fraser T Smith
notes: British guitarist-turned-producer spanning chart pop and UK rap/grime. The Lane line names the rap-facing work first and gives it the half-time class — "the rap-facing work is half-time (backbeat on 3) at 130—145 and the pop work is 2&4 straight at 70—120" — so `halfTime` is true at `halftime_3` on the 130—145 band, with the pop mode documented rather than blended. Because the placement matches the parent, the separation is the UK-rap skeleton the entry spells out: "a UK-rap skeleton of sparse kick, clap on 3, and 16th/32nd hats. Percussion is dry and forward on the rap records, wet on the pop records." So the kick density falls to 1—3, the roll vocabulary is 32nd-led at a high frequency, the snare is a `short`-reverb clap with a `hard` transient, and the perc gain is the most forward on the producer side of this section. "His rap productions leave large amounts of space for the vocal" is the low melody `densityPerBar` and the raised `emptyBarBias`. The 808 is authored because the entry names it and calls it the mode marker: "808 sub with short glides on the rap records; sustained synth or electric bass on the pop records. The low end is the main thing that differentiates his two modes." So `bass808` is `counter_riff` and the bassline is the sustained synth half at a very high `followRootsProb`. Harmony is "minor keys with gospel and grime-derived colour — plagal cadences, suspended voicings, and a taste for a single sustained chord under a rap verse", which is the tonic family at real weight, `susSubstitutionProb` 0.42 and a long `chordDurationBeats` window; "piano, strings and guitar over 4- or 8-bar minor loops" with "countermelody is a string line or a picked guitar figure" is the `sustain_pad`/`answer_lick` pair. ⚠ `confidence` is medium and the research says why: "parametric detail partly inferred", with its own [LOW-CONF] mark on the guitarist-idiomatic voicing claim repeated here. Every drum probability, the humanize numbers and `bpm.mode` 137 (the midpoint of the stated 130—145 rap band) are INFERRED. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“808 sub with short glides on the rap records; sustained synth or electric bass on the pop records. The low end is the main thing that differentiates his two modes.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord.
